newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak crown firms in quiet trade, seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Slovak crown firms in quiet trade, seen steady.

text.p: The Slovak crown firmed in quiet morning trade on Friday and dealers said they expected it to stay steady throughout the day.
The crown traded at -1.50 percent on the depreciation side of its mark/dollar basket parity at 0800 GMT, up from the opening -2.0 percent versus the midpoint.
"We think the crown will hold steady, or slightly firm, later in the day as the central bank is very likely to keep its strong fixing," said one Bratislava-based trader.
"The NBS has made it clear enough it wants the crown at around its fixing levels so the market will move towards it sooner or later," he added.
The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) has been fixing the crown stronger than market levels over the past two weeks to support the currency against speculative pressure.

On Thursday, the NBS fixed the crown at 33.313 to the dollar and at 19.544 to the mark, implying a deviation against the basket of -0.67 percent. The crown was trading at around -3.0 percent versus the basket shortly before the fixing.
But dealers noted both Slovak foreign exchange and money markets remained tight and that local banks could quote only limited volumes.
"It will take some time till we will return to normal trading, the market is still stagnant as funds are simply not available there at the moment," said Tibor Fratrik of ING Bank.
The NBS also deliberately keeps the market short of liquidity to prevent access to crown funds that could be used for speculative selling and spark a fall in the crown.
The NBS said it would hold a three-day repo tender on Friday, but offered only a fixed amount of one billion crowns.
The central bank has said it would continue its strategy of keeping the market short of crown funds to prevent pressure on the currency.
According to NBS figures the Slovak banking sector lacked 7.14 percent of required funds to meet minimum reserves requirements as of May 29.
